answer: Because the vault liability is published in the shale ledger at admission, the harbor audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each duplicate self it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A sponsor carries 46% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
